ca_snake_head_boulder.blurb: Snake Head Boulder is the largest cluster of problems in Valley of the Dolls, a bouldering zone on Sugarloaf Mountain within the Box Springs Mountain Reserve above Riverside. It has nine problems, all on granite and all fairly approachable: six at VB, two at V0 and one at V2. The boulder stands on the hillside above a big water tank, and the setting gives wide views over the surrounding valley. Getting there takes a steady uphill hike beyond the Valley of the Dolls trail, so bring crash pads you are happy to carry. It suits climbers working through easy and moderate problems.

ca_intergalactic_odyssey_boulder.blurb: Intergalactic Odyssey Boulder is a single granite boulder with nine problems, found on a plateau in the Intergalactic Hustle Area of Belvedere Heights, on the southwest side of Box Springs Mountain above Riverside. The problems cover a wide spread: five at VB or V0, a couple at V1, then single problems around V3 and V5, so both newer boulderers and stronger climbers have something to try. One problem has a sit start. The plateau sits well above the trailhead, and the walk in is a real hike with a steep final stretch, so plan on carrying pads uphill.

ca_left_of_amphitheater.blurb: Left of Amphitheater is the westernmost section of The Mill, a basalt crag on the rim above Mill Creek Canyon in northeast California, at about 3,000 feet. Nine routes mix four trad lines, three sport routes and two top-ropes, with grades from 5.9 up to the low 5.13 range; some of the harder lines are still projects. From the top of the approach trail you head left over a talus field, and the routes begin around a corner.

ca_right_of_alcove.blurb: Right of Alcove is a stretch of basalt wall at The Mill, on the rim above Mill Creek Canyon in northeast California, running from the Alcove toward the Goonies Buttress. Nine routes, mostly traditional: eight trad lines and one sport route. Most fall in the 5.10 range, with one easier line near 5.8 and a few that reach 5.11 and 5.12. Climbs include crack and roof features, and a couple go to two pitches. From the top of the approach trail, turn right and continue beyond the alcove; the wall carries on past a big step under a tree. It suits climbers comfortable placing gear on steady 5.10 terrain.

ca_boulder_2_5.blurb: Boulder 2 is a small boulder in the Lonely Stones group of Joshua Tree National Park, just east of Dream Sequence Boulder and Boulder 3. It holds nine easy problems: five at VB, two at V0 and two at V1, so it works as a gentle stop for beginners or as a warm-up. The north face carries a dark patina. The boulders in this group are large enough that some side is usually in shade, though the area itself is open and exposed. The walk in is about half a mile.
ca_boulder_2_5.parking_note: Use the first paved turnout on the right once you are in the park, about 0.4 miles along the road.
ca_boulder_2_5.approach: Cross the road to a faint trail and keep right at the fork about 450 feet along. Continue roughly half a mile to the southeast.

ca_brain_stem_rock.blurb: Brain Stem Rock is a large split boulder beside the Fry Koegel Trail on Mount Woodson in northern San Diego County. It holds nine routes: four sport, four trad and one aid line. Grades run from 5.8 through the 5.10s, with a couple at 5.11 and one at the low end of 5.12, and the climbing includes a slab and arete, a chimney start and an offwidth. It is a compact spot for a mixed session of bolts and gear, reached by a hike on the trail from the road.

ca_t_j_swan_cliff.blurb: T J Swan Cliff is a small west-facing cliff beside T J Lake, at about 9,350 feet in the Mammoth Lakes area of the Eastern Sierra. It has nine routes on volcanic rock: five sport, two trad and two alpine-style lines, running from 5.6 or so up to 5.10. Most climbs are easy angled, and a top-rope can be rigged from the bolts or with gear, so it is a sound choice for newer leaders and for families. From the lake, go left and walk around its shoreline clockwise; the cliff soon appears.
